# Bob

Bob is a self-improving AI system based on Pi agent.  

```
stack.yaml ──generate-*──▶ config/* ──mount──▶ model-server / pi
                │
                └──download──▶ models/*.gguf
```

## Control surface

All day-to-day operations go through `ctl.sh`. Run `./ctl.sh help` for the full
command list.

## Quick start

Edit only `stack.yaml`, then:

```bash
cd /home/master/src/bob

./ctl.sh generate-config
./ctl.sh generate-pi-config
./ctl.sh download
./ctl.sh start
```

Useful checks:

```bash
./ctl.sh status            # local presence + bytes
./ctl.sh status --verify   # also compare against Hugging Face sizes
./ctl.sh logs              # model-server logs
./ctl.sh stop
```

Run the agent (interactive TUI, bind-mounts CWD to /workspace):

```bash
./ctl.sh pi
```

Rebuild agent images (base → pi) with `./ctl.sh rebuild-agents`.

## Repository layout

```
bob/
├── ctl.sh                           # control surface — start here
├── stack.yaml                       # single source of truth
├── AGENTS.md                        # agent session entrypoint
├── config/
│   ├── config.generated.ini         # model-server preset (mounted as /config/config.ini)
│   └── pi/{models,settings}.json    # Pi agent config
├── models/<model-dir>/*.gguf
├── scripts/                         # ctl.sh command implementations + bootstrap.py
├── docker/                          # base + agent + downloader images
├── docker-compose.yaml
└── docs/                            # lifecycle docs + detailed reference
```

## Architecture

```
model-server ──network──▶ model-downloader (profile: download)
      │
      └── OpenAI-compat──▶ pi (profile: pi)
```

- **model-server** — llama.cpp; reads generated `config.generated.ini`
- **model-downloader** — fetches GGUF/mmproj files (opt-in profile)
- **pi** — Pi coding agent on `bob-agent-base`; config from `stack.yaml`

# Pentest Guide — Interactive Walkthrough

## Quick Start

```bash
cd pentest
npm install
node cli/cli.js
```

## Stage 1: Reconnaissance

Reconnaissance identifies the target application's structure, tech stack, and exposed endpoints. Use `pento recon <url>` to run this stage.

**What we test:**
- Page title, meta tags (description, keywords)
- Favicon presence
- JavaScript file sources (React/Vue framework detection)
- API endpoints via route interception

**Output:** Saved to `outputs/recon.txt`

---

## Stage 2: Vulnerability Scanning (OWASP TOP 10)

Vulnerability scanning probes for known attack patterns using Playwright automation. Use `pento vuln <url>` to run this stage.

**What we test:**
- A01 — SQL Injection (test payloads, error responses)
- A02 — Broken Authentication (session hijacking via insecure cookies)
- A04 — Cross-Site Scripting (reflected XSS in search boxes)
- A05 — Broken Access Control (IDOR by ID manipulation)

**Output:** Saved to `outputs/vuln.txt`

---

## Stage 3: Exploitation

Exploitation delivers proof-of-concept payloads to demonstrate active vulnerabilities. Use `pento exploit <url>` to run this stage.

**What we test:**
- SQL injection with UNION-based data extraction
- XSS payload execution in DOM context

**Output:** Saved to `outputs/exploit.txt`

---

## Stage 4: Analysis & Remediation

Analysis evaluates findings and recommends remediation steps. Use `pento analyze <url>` to run this stage.

**What we analyze:**
- Severity scoring and risk assessment
- Root cause identification
- Remediation advice per vulnerability type

**Output:** Saved to `outputs/analyze.txt`

---

## Stage 5: Report Generation

Report generation compiles all findings into a structured output. Use `pento report <url>` to run this stage.

**What we generate:**
- HTML report (webviewable)
- Markdown report (documentation-ready)
- JSON results (machine-parseable)

**Output:** Saved to `outputs/report.txt` and `outputs/` folder

---

## Architecture Overview

```
┌─────────────┐   ┌─────────────┐   ┌─────────────┐
│  Recon      │──▶│ Vulnerability│──▶│ Exploitation│
│  (Discover) │   │   Scan      │   │   (POC)     │
└─────────────┘   └─────────────┘   └─────────────┘
        │                    │
        ▼                    ▼
┌─────────────┐   ┌─────────────┐
│ Analysis    │──▶│  Report     │
│  (Advice)   │   │  Generation │
└─────────────┘   └─────────────┘
```

---

## Contributing — Adding New Test Cases

To add a new vulnerability test case:

1. Create `src/vuln/<VulnName>.ts` with `test<Name>()` function
2. Export the result type interface
3. Update `docs/guide.md` to document the test
4. Register in the orchestrator (`src/core/orchestrator.ts`)

Each test case should:
- Accept a Playwright `Page` and target URL
- Return an object with `vulnType`, `severity`, `description`, `status`, `evidence`, and `stepsToReproduce`
- Be executable in ~30 seconds max

---

## Next Steps — Building Out the Tool

- [ ] Wire Playwright into actual test implementations
- [ ] Add more OWASP TOP 10 tests (A06, A07, A08, A09, A10)
- [ ] Generate HTML/Markdown reports from scan results
- [ ] Add interactive CLI using `readline-sync` prompts
- [ ] Integrate Nuclei/ZAP for faster scanning
# Pentest Suite — Documentation Framework

## Overview

This project is a full-stack, end-to-end automated web application penetration testing suite built with TypeScript/JavaScript, Playwright, and a modular CLI tool. It covers all OWASP TOP 10 attack vectors, from reconnaissance through exploitation to analysis and reporting.

## Interactive Guide

The interactive guide lives at `docs/guide.md` — it loads dynamically from the docs folder. Each command (`pento recon`, `pento vuln`, etc.) prints a help message pointing to the relevant guide section in `docs/guide.md`. When implemented, the CLI will load and render the full guide interactively using `readline-sync`.

## Project Structure

```
pentest/
├── docs/                     # Documentation (guide + reference)
│   ├── index.md              # Entry point for interactive guide
│   ├── guide.md              # Full interactive walkthrough
│   └── spec/
│       ├── recon.md          # Reconnaissance phase specs
│       ├── vuln.md           # Vulnerability scanning specs
│       ├── exploit.md        # Exploitation & payload specs
│       ├── analyze.md        # Findings analysis specs
│       └── report.md         # Reporting specs
├── src/
│   ├── cli/                  # CLI implementation
│   ├── core/                 # Core engine (pipeline, runner)
│   ├── vuln/                 # OWASP TOP 10 test cases
│   ├── exploit/             # Payload delivery & exploitation
│   ├── analyze/             # Findings analysis
│   └── report/              # Report generation
├── config/
│   └── test-suite.yaml       # Stage definitions + thresholds
└── cli/
    └── cli.js                # Entry point
```

## Quick Start

```bash
cd pentest
npm install
node cli/cli.js init      # Initialize project with defaults
```

## Phase-by-Phase Guide

Each phase has its own spec document in `docs/spec/`. See `docs/guide.md` for the full interactive walkthrough.
